## Findings
- claim-1: For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), put \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). The two displayed Schur-function sets generate \(J_v\) integrally as an ideal of \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), and each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2@L1380-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The paper conjectures these two generating sets are minimal; it reports finite verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1489-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Let \(R\) be a commutative unital ring, \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\Lambda_d\) a connected graded \(R\)-algebra (\(\Lambda_0=R\)), and \(M=\bigoplus_{d\ge N_0}M_d\) a bounded-below graded \(\Lambda\)-module. For homogeneous \(m_1,\ldots,m_t\), they generate \(M\) iff their images generate \(Q:=M/\Lambda_+M\) over \(R\). Proof: the forward implication is immediate. Conversely, induct on degree \(d\). Modulo \(\Lambda_+M\), a homogeneous \(m\in M_d\) is an \(R\)-linear combination of the \(m_i\) of degree \(d\); the difference lies in \(\sum_{e>0}\Lambda_eM_{d-e}\), whose module factors have smaller degree and hence lie in the generated submodule by induction.
- claim-4: Under the preceding hypotheses, a homogeneous generating set of \(M\) is inclusion-minimal iff its image is an inclusion-minimal \(R\)-spanning set of \(Q\). Apply the previous claim to every subset obtained by deleting generators.
- claim-5: If \(A\) is a quotient of \(\Lambda\), \(M\subseteq A\) is an ideal, and \(S\subseteq M\), then \(S\) generates \(M\) as an \(A\)-ideal iff it generates \(M\) as a \(\Lambda\)-module. This follows from surjectivity \(\Lambda\to A\).
- claim-6: Consequently, for the integral \(J_v\), if \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) requires \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators as an abelian group, then each of the two \(N\)-element sets above is inclusion-minimal. This proves the conditional indecomposables reduction.
- claim-7: The stronger condition \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^N\) implies the preceding generator-number condition. More generally, for nonzero \(R\), if \(Q\cong R^N\), every \(N\)-element spanning set is minimal: localizing at a maximal ideal and reducing modulo it shows that fewer than \(N\) elements cannot span.
- claim-8: For a finitely generated abelian group \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^r\oplus T\), \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=r+\max_p\dim_{\mathbb F_p}(T/pT)\). Thus torsion can increase the required number of indecomposables; rank alone does not determine it.
- claim-9: Inclusion-minimal spanning sets need not have a ring-independent or even \(\mathbb Z\)-module-independent common cardinality: \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2,3\}\) are both inclusion-minimal generating sets of \(\mathbb Z/6\). Hence the abstract reduction proves inclusion-minimality of the specified sets under \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=N\), but does not justify a general assertion that all minimal sets have equal size.
- claim-10: For scalar extension defined algebraically by \(\Lambda_R=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\) and \(M_R=M_{\mathbb Z}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\), one has \(M_R/(\Lambda_R)_+M_R\cong Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\); right-exactness suffices, so no flatness is needed. If \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\), this becomes \(R^N\), giving minimality over every nonzero \(R\). If \(Q\) has torsion, base change can kill indecomposables, so integral minimality does not automatically transfer.
- claim-11: The stronger freeness statement \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) is conjectural in the source, which states that a proof had eluded the authors. [source-2@L1517-L1552|claim=formal-document]
## Strategy
- Work integrally. Let \(\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\) be connected nonnegatively graded, \(A=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}/I\), and let \(J_v\subseteq A\) be graded, with its \(\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\)-action induced by \(\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\twoheadrightarrow A\). Put \(\Lambda_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}\Lambda_d\) and \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\).
- Prove graded Nakayama by induction from the lower degree bound: homogeneous elements generate \(J_v\) iff their images span \(Q\) over \(\mathbb Z\). Applying this to each deletion proves equivalence of inclusion-minimality upstairs and downstairs.
- By claim-1, each displayed Schur set is a homogeneous integral generating set of cardinality
  \[
  N=\binom{a+b}{a}.
  \]
  Therefore, conditional on \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=N\), neither set admits a deletion: otherwise \(Q\) would be generated by \(N-1\) elements. This establishes the conditional reduction, not the conjectural hypothesis.
- For finitely generated \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^r\oplus T\),
  \[
  \mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=r+\max_p\dim_{\mathbb F_p}(T/pT).
  \]
  The lower bound follows from \(Q/pQ\); the upper bound follows by arranging the cyclic primary factors of \(T\) into \(\max_p\dim(T/pT)\) invariant-factor generators. Thus rank alone is insufficient.
- For abstract scalar extension \(J_R=J_v\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\),
  \[
  J_R/(\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\otimes R)_+J_R\cong Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R.
  \]
  This follows by tensoring the right-exact sequence \(\Lambda_+J_v\to J_v\to Q\to0\); no flatness is required. If \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\) and \(R\ne0\), this quotient is \(R^N\), which cannot be spanned by fewer than \(N\) elements after reduction modulo a maximal ideal.

## Gaps
- The required hypothesis
  \[
  \mu_{\mathbb Z}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)=\binom{a+b}{a}
  \]
  is unresolved. Claim-11 records it as conjectural; freeness \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\) is also unresolved.
- Torsion in \(Q\) can raise \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)\) above its rank, so a rank computation cannot prove the conditional hypothesis.
- Abstract \(J_v\otimes R\) need not inject into \(A\otimes R\) for nonflat \(R\). Consequently it cannot automatically be identified with either its image ideal or a geometrically defined coefficient-\(R\) ideal.
- If \(Q\) has torsion, base change may kill or alter indecomposables. Integral minimality therefore does not automatically transfer to arbitrary coefficient rings.

## Next
- Produce an integral presentation of \(Q\) from Schur multiplication and compute its Smith normal form, or prove matching lower bounds for \(\dim_{\mathbb F_p}(Q/pQ)\) for every relevant prime.
- Separately establish torsion-freeness if the stronger free-\(\mathbb Z^N\) statement is sought.
- For geometric coefficient change, prove an appropriate flatness/injectivity or geometric base-change comparison before applying the abstract scalar-extension result.
